title: A mechanism for hypoxia-induced inflammatory cell death in cancer
source: Science TLDR podcast episode 13 show notes
one_line: Defines a PTP1B-RNF213-CYLD/SPATA2 pathway that drives NF-kB activation, NLRP3 inflammasome induction and pyroptotic death of hypoxic cancer cells.
key_claims: PTP1B inhibition activates the E3 ligase RNF213, with ABL1/2-mediated tyrosine phosphorylation at Tyr-1275 controlling RNF213 oligomerization and RZ domain activation.
The RNF213 RZ domain ubiquitylates CYLD and SPATA2, negative regulators of NF-kB, driving their degradation, while the RING domain negatively regulates RZ activity.
CYLD/SPATA2 loss activates NF-kB and induces the NLRP3 inflammasome, which together with hypoxia-induced ER stress triggers pyroptosis.
Pyroptosis, marked by GSDMD and inflammatory caspase activity, is the primary death mode in hypoxic PTP1B-deficient cancer cells, distinct from apoptosis, necroptosis and ferroptosis.
Xenograft experiments deleting or mutating PTP1B, CYLD, NLRP3 and RNF213 validated the pathway's effect on tumour growth, nominating PTP1B, CYLD/SPATA2 and NLRP3 as therapeutic targets.
limitations: Full substrate specificity of the RNF213 RING versus RZ domains, and their interplay, was not characterized.
The pathway's role in normal tissues under hypoxia was not examined.
The mechanism of LUBAC contribution to CYLD/SPATA2 degradation and its relation to RZ activity remains unresolved.
In vivo evidence rests on xenograft models rather than immunocompetent or autochthonous tumour settings.
No targeted therapeutic agent against the pathway was developed or tested.
open_questions: Do PTP1B inhibitors, CYLD/SPATA2-targeting agents or NLRP3 antagonists shrink hypoxic tumours in immunocompetent models?
Does mutating RNF213 Tyr-1275 alone abolish pyroptosis in vivo, isolating the phosphorylation step as causal?
Does this pathway explain RNF213's established role in Moyamoya disease and other inflammatory/autoimmune conditions?
